title: A project installation: the owned root in the project, referred to from omp's project plugin directory
situation: Install, owned root and uninstall now carry two installation scopes, user and project, with a project's installation taking precedence inside it. omp 18.12.1 loads extension packages from the user's plugin directory and from a project's, `<anchor>/.omp/plugins` (the nearest ancestor holding `.omp/`, the home's excluded, else the nearest holding `.git`), and a project package shadows a user package of the same name (its plugin loader, read in the shipped binary). A project's plugin links live under `node_modules`, which most projects ignore. The author's render tree also defaults to `.cratylus/<harness>` in the project it is run in.
decision: (1) install and uninstall take `--scope user|project`, user by default; on a terminal install asks for the scope it is not told, user preselected, wherever the project resolved from the working directory is not the home; `--yes` or no terminal takes user. (2) The project is the one omp anchors its plugins at from the working directory: the nearest ancestor holding `.omp/` other than the home, else the nearest holding `.git`, else the working directory; project scope is refused where that is the home. (3) A project's owned root is `<project>/.cratylus/<harness>`, laid out as the user's, and its installation record states its scope. (4) Its references are in `<project>/.omp/plugins`, each relative so a clone elsewhere resolves them: a link `node_modules/cratylus-omp` to the root, a dependency entry naming the root by a relative `file:` path in that directory's `package.json`, and, in that directory's `.gitignore`, the lines that re-include that one link for a project ignoring `node_modules`. Same package name as the user's, so omp loads only the project's in that project. (5) At project scope the settings install reads and writes, the models of tiers and roles and the status line choice, are the project's `.omp/config.yml`. (6) A project install or uninstall writes nothing under the home: no earlier-installation migration, no user settings. (7) The version-skew warning and report name the scope and root of the installation in use, and the remedy names its scope. (8) The operator's command, with no installation named, reads the nearest project installation above the working directory, else the user's. (9) A project root and an author's render tree never share a directory: install refuses a project root over a `.cratylus/<harness>` holding files and no installation record, and `project` refuses to render into a directory holding one.
consequences: Three builders: install and uninstall at both scopes; version skew and the runtime's choice of installation; the command reference and help, which also drop what is left of Claude Code. A team commits `.cratylus/<harness>` and `.omp/` to share the installation; every teammate's omp loads it.
